stories.title: Ambrose Breaks Ground on Two Facilities at Indianapolis Logistics Park
stories.excerpt: Ambrose has broken ground on two buildings at the Indianapolis Logistics Park – Northwest, a 104-acre modern industrial park in Whitestown, Indiana, part of Greater Indianapolis. The two buildings are being developed on a speculative basis and are designed to accommodate a range of industrial uses, totaling approximately 947,000 square feet. The construction of the properties marks the commencement of the second phase of the park’s master-planned development. This milestone follows the recent disposition of one of the property’s buildings, which is fully leased to a global healthcare services and products company. The park’s other existing buildings are also fully occupied by Safavieh, KattSafe, Royal Interpack and Amazon. The general contractor on the project is Compass Commercial Construction, with design services provided by Curran Architecture and Kimley-Horn. The Indianapolis-based Colliers International team is managing leasing and marketing for the property. Ambrose has partnered with Fifth Third Bank on the construction loan. The post Ambrose Breaks Ground on Two Facilities at Indianapolis Logistics Park appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Ambrose breaks ground on 947K SF across two buildings at Indianapolis Logistics Park Northwest.
Existing park fully leased to Amazon, Safavieh, KattSafe, Royal Interpack, and healthcare company.
Fifth Third Bank financing; Colliers managing leasing for speculative phase-two industrial development.
stories.summary: Ambrose has commenced phase two of the Indianapolis Logistics Park Northwest with two speculative industrial buildings totaling 947,000 square feet in Whitestown. The existing buildings at the 104-acre park are fully occupied by major tenants including Amazon and a global healthcare services company. Construction financing is backed by Fifth Third Bank with Colliers handling leasing and marketing.
stories.impact: Growing speculative industrial activity in greater Indianapolis signals confidence in demand from logistics and healthcare tenants; full occupancy of existing buildings and phase-two groundbreak suggest strong absorption in the I-465 corridor, reducing risk for future multifamily demand tied to warehouse employment and population retention.

stories.title: BIG 4 Alliance Partners with Supply Chain Federation, CREDA SoCal
stories.excerpt: The BIG 4, an alliance between the cities of Commerce, Industry, Santa Fe Springs, and Vernon, announced on Monday a new partnership with the Supply Chain Federation, a national advocacy organization representing business and labor in goods movement, and CREDA SoCal to advance a regional approach to industrial development, workforce opportunity and supply-chain resilience across Southern California. As its first major initiative, the partnership will host the second annual BIG 4 Summit in 2027, bringing together regional and national stakeholders to advance conversations around industrial development, supply-chain resilience, workforce opportunity, economic competitiveness, industrial land, infrastructure and public-private collaboration. Since its formation in October 2025, the BIG 4 has established a unified voice for the shared interests and needs of its four cities and worked to expand business opportunities in the region through streamlined permitting, tax incentives, low-interest financing and reduced energy costs. In its first year, the BIG 4 has launched business incentives, convened the inaugural BIG 4 Summit, advocated for SB 1274 and closed its first joint economic development deal, keeping 80-year-old Juanita’s Foods and its manufacturing operations in Southern California. The post BIG 4 Alliance Partners with Supply Chain Federation, CREDA SoCal appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: BIG 4 alliance (Commerce, Industry, Santa Fe Springs, Vernon) partners with Supply Chain Federation and CREDA SoCal.
First year achievements: streamlined permitting, tax incentives, 80-year-old Juanita's Foods retained in SoCal.
2027 BIG 4 Summit to convene regional stakeholders on industrial development, supply-chain resilience, workforce.
stories.summary: The BIG 4 alliance of four Southern California cities has partnered with the Supply Chain Federation to advance regional industrial development and workforce opportunity. Since October 2025, the alliance has launched business incentives, secured the Juanita's Foods manufacturing deal, and advocated for SB 1274. The partnership will host the 2027 BIG 4 Summit to strengthen supply-chain resilience and industrial competitiveness across the region.
stories.impact: Coordinated industrial incentives (permitting, tax breaks, low-cost energy, financing) in LA County's Commerce/Industry cluster will anchor manufacturing and logistics employment, stabilizing renter bases and supporting multifamily demand in these underserved, cost-competitive submarkets; retention of legacy tenants signals policy commitment to prevent industrial flight.

stories.title: JLL Selected to Lead Leasing at 165-Acre Industrial Site in Cleveland
stories.excerpt: JLL will serve as the exclusive leasing agent for Commerce Park 71, a 165-acre industrial development in Burbank, Ohio. The site offers exceptional power capacity—more than 200 megawatts—along Northeast Ohio’s I-71 corridor. The property’s flexible design allows it to be divided into parcels as small as five acres, accommodating a diverse range of industrial users from large-scale distribution centers to advanced manufacturing. JLL Executive Managing Director Joe Messina, Managing Director David Stecker and Associate Joe Warren are representing the park owner, WCP. “Commerce Park 71 checks many of the boxes today’s industrial users are looking for, particularly those with significant power requirements,” said Stecker.” Commerce Park 71 also offers convenient access to major Midwest markets through its direct connection to Interstate 71. The site is approximately 45 minutes from downtown Cleveland and 35 minutes from Cleveland-Hopkins International Airport, with Columbus just 80 miles to the south. Chicago, Cincinnati, Detroit, Indianapolis, Pittsburgh, and other major regional markets are all within a five-hour drive. The post JLL Selected to Lead Leasing at 165-Acre Industrial Site in Cleveland appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: JLL leasing Commerce Park 71: 165 acres, 200+ MW power capacity, I-71 corridor near Cleveland.
Flexible parcels (5+ acres); 45 minutes from Cleveland, 35 minutes from Hopkins Airport, 80 miles to Columbus.
Target users: large distribution, advanced manufacturing with significant power requirements in Northeast Ohio.
stories.summary: Commerce Park 71, a 165-acre industrial site in Burbank, Ohio along I-71, is being marketed exclusively by JLL. The property offers more than 200 megawatts of power capacity and flexible parceling starting at five acres, positioning it for large-scale distribution and advanced manufacturing. The site enjoys strategic proximity to Cleveland, Columbus, and major Midwest markets within a five-hour radius.
stories.impact: Exceptional power infrastructure and modular design target data centers and advanced manufacturing, which typically require smaller footprints than traditional logistics; if power-hungry tenants (AI, semiconductors) locate at Commerce Park 71, Northeast Ohio's I-71 corridor gains inflow of higher-wage jobs and younger workforce, strengthening multifamily demand in Cleveland and Columbus submarkets ahead of competitive supply.

stories.title: Catholic Charities Cuts Ribbon on $143M Affordable Seniors Housing in Brownsville
stories.excerpt: City and state officials joined representatives from Catholic Charities and community leaders to cut the ribbon on the new Catholic Charities Gail P. Duke Senior Residence. This $143.4-million development will provide 141 units of affordable sustainable apartments for low-income seniors with supportive services in the Brownsville neighborhood of Brooklyn. The Gail P. Duke Senior Residence, which began construction in 2024, was developed by Catholic Charities Progress of Peoples Development Corporation, the affordable housing arm of the Diocese of Brooklyn. Construction financing included 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits supported by $84,715,000 in NYC Housing Development Corporation Tax-Exempt Bonds and syndicated by Richman Housing Resources. “More senior housing units are needed in all five boroughs across the city to house our fellow New Yorkers, and developments like the Gail P. Duke Senior Residence are exactly the type of project which is helping us cover that gap,” said New York City Department of Buildings Commissioner Ahmed Tigani. The post Catholic Charities Cuts Ribbon on $143M Affordable Seniors Housing in Brownsville appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Catholic Charities opens $143.4M Gail P. Duke Senior Residence: 141 affordable units in Brownsville, Brooklyn.
Financing: $84.7M NYC Housing Development Corporation tax-exempt bonds plus 4% LIHTC.
City confirms gap in senior housing across all five boroughs; project addresses critical affordable inventory shortage.
stories.summary: The $143.4 million Gail P. Duke Senior Residence opened in Brownsville, Brooklyn, delivering 141 affordable units for low-income seniors with supportive services. Construction began in 2024 and was funded via $84.7 million in NYC HDP tax-exempt bonds and 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits syndicated by Richman Housing Resources. City officials noted acute shortage of senior housing across all five boroughs.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to market-rate multifamily development; however, acknowledged senior housing gap citywide signals underinvestment and pent-up demand for age-targeted communities, creating an opening for market-rate senior rental/assisted living development in outer-borough growth corridors (Queens, Bronx) where land costs and density tolerance are higher than Manhattan/Brooklyn core.

stories.title: Gavigan’s Furniture Buys Maryland Warehouse for $18M
stories.excerpt: Gavigan’s Furniture has acquired 700 Evelyn Avenue, a 177,536-square-foot warehouse in Maryland, for $17.75 million. Gavigan’s Furniture previously leased the asset, located in the Linthicum section of Anne Arundel County, to house warehouse operations and administrative offices. Matthew Curran, SIOR and Andrew Meeder, SIOR, Senior Vice Presidents and Principals at MacKenzie Commercial Real Estate Services, LLC, represented the buyer. “Gavigan’s Furniture has occupied 700 Evelyn Avenue for more than a decade as a tenant, and this acquisition allows the company to transition from tenant to owner-occupant,” said MacKenzie’s Curran. “Ownership gives the company greater control over its long-term operating and occupancy costs while providing a foundation for future expansion.” Built in 1968 and also known as the Commerce Corporation Building, the building features 25 loading docks, nine drive-in bays, and a second-level office component. The site is directly adjacent to Interstates 695 and 895, and is located near BWI Airport and the Port of Baltimore. The post Gavigan’s Furniture Buys Maryland Warehouse for $18M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Gavigan's Furniture acquires 177.5K SF warehouse in Linthicum, Anne Arundel County, Maryland for $17.75M.
Property adjacent I-695/I-895 interchange, near BWI Airport and Port of Baltimore; 25 loading docks, 9 bays.
Tenant transitions to owner-occupant after 10+ years of lease; controls long-term costs, enables expansion.
stories.summary: Gavigan's Furniture has purchased the 700 Evelyn Avenue warehouse, a 177,536-square-foot facility in Anne Arundel County, Maryland, for $17.75 million. The company occupied the asset as a tenant for over a decade and now owns the building, which features 25 loading docks, nine drive-in bays, and direct access to I-695 and I-895 near BWI and Baltimore's port. Ownership provides cost certainty and expansion flexibility.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact; warehouse automation and owner-occupant transitions in industrial parks typically reduce net job growth relative to leased facilities, which tend to churn more rapidly and attract diverse tenants—key risk if Baltimore/Anne Arundel County industrial base consolidates around long-term owner-operators rather than high-turnover logistics.

stories.title: Sunday Summary: Welcome Back, Speyer!
stories.excerpt: Back in 1997, one of the storied New York City real estate firms — Tishman Speyer — purchased one of the storied New York City properties: the Chrysler Building. Well, technically, what Tishman Speyer purchased was the skyscraper’s ground lease. The site was still owned by Cooper Union. Moreover, it was a ground lease that would get progressively more expensive in the coming years. (Shrewdly, Tishman Speyer sold a 90 percent interest in the building to the Abu Dhabi Investment Council in 2008 for $800 million.) When the property went up for sale again in 2019, expectations were significantly lowered about the value of the deal, given that the yearly payments to Cooper Union had by then ballooned from $7.8 million a year to $32.5 million. Still, market observers figured Chrysler was iconic, eye-catching, centrally located and beloved enough to fetch at least $500 million. After all, how many other properties of such status go on the market every day? But, when the ground rent was factored in, along with the fact that the property was in need of serious updates and repairs, the offers started coming in far, far lower than hoped for. The winning bid from RFR Realty was only $150 million. However, even that discounted price might have been too much. It wasn’t long before RFR and Cooper Union began butting heads about missed rent payments, necessary improvements and more. (RFR also had the poor luck of closing the deal in 2019, just before the office market was about to go into deep freeze.) RFR was eventually pushed out, and Cooper Union began looking around again for a savior. They apparently found one last week in the form of … Tishman Speyer? How much Tishman paid is still unknown, but the preliminary details indicate that the new land lease will last 150 years, and Tishman is putting up $235 million for improvements to the property. “We are pursuing an ambitious plan for the Chrysler Building at a historically strong moment for the Manhattan office market,” Rob Spey
bullets: Chrysler Building (NYC): Tishman Speyer ground-lease payment escalated from $7.8M (1997) to $32.5M (2019).
2019 sales expectations undershot due to escalating rent burden and deferred capital needs despite iconic status.
Article incomplete; reflects structural challenges in high-value trophy properties constrained by legacy lease structures.
stories.summary: Tishman Speyer's experience with the Chrysler Building illustrates the hazard of ground leases with escalating rent obligations. After purchasing the skyscraper's ground lease in 1997 (with Cooper Union as fee owner), annual payments ballooned from $7.8 million to $32.5 million by 2019, severely constraining the property's value despite its iconic status and prime Manhattan location. The article implies market expectations for resale were significantly dampened by this lease burden.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily development; however, serves as cautionary tale for developers considering ground-leased multifamily sites—escalating rent obligations can erode NOI and residual land value, making it critical to model long-term lease economics and fee-simple acquisition risk before underwriting.

stories.title: Charter School Inks 56K-SF Lease in Retail Center Near Miami Suburb
stories.excerpt: Charter school network BridgePrep Academy will open another location, this time inside a shopping center in Miami-Dade County. The school operator, which has 19 locations across Florida, signed a 56,000-square-foot lease at the open-air California Club Shopping Center in Ives Estates, near Aventura, 15 miles north of Downtown Miami. The 273,050-square-foot property, owned by RK Centers, sits west of Interstate 95 at 750 Ives Dairy Road. Other tenants at California Club include Planet Fitness, Five Below and Burlington. Waterways Preparatory Academy @ Kropp Annex, part of the public Dade County School District, previously leased BridgePrep’s new space up until at least last year. “Miami doesn’t have a surplus of properties that work for educational operators,” CBRE’s Scott Goldstein, who represented the tenant alongside Keith Edelman, said in a statement. “We moved quickly.” Some of the challenges include the lack of available properties that have the correct code and layout. Demand for grade schools, mostly for private ones, has skyrocketed in South Florida since the onset of the pandemic, when a slew of new-market companies opened offices and their employees moved in tow. To fix the issue, billionaire developer Stephen Ross is donating $100 million to Pine Crest School, a private school with locations in Fort Lauderdale and Boca Raton, to open another in West Palm Beach, Bloomberg reported. Another billionaire, Jeff Greene, has spent $50 million to build The Greene School, also in West Palm Beach, the Wall Street Journal reported. BridgePrep Academy and RK Centers did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: BridgePrep Academy signs 56K SF lease at California Club Shopping Center, Ives Estates, Miami-Dade County.
Charter network operates 19 Florida locations; tenant cite shortage of properties with correct educational code/layout.
Ives Estates location 15 miles north of Downtown Miami; property includes Planet Fitness, Five Below, Burlington.
stories.summary: Charter school operator BridgePrep Academy has leased 56,000 square feet at the California Club Shopping Center in Ives Estates, Miami-Dade County, marking its newest location among 19 Florida sites. CBRE brokers noted acute shortage of properties meeting educational code and layout requirements. The 273,050-square-foot open-air center is west of I-95 and home to Planet Fitness, Five Below, and Burlington.
stories.impact: Private school expansion in South Florida signals post-pandemic sustained demand for K-12 alternatives; inflow of charter and private school operators (particularly in suburban Miami-Dade north of Downtown) drives young-family renter demand in Aventura, Ives Estates, and Broward corridors, supporting multifamily development targeting 30–45-year-old household formations with school-age children.

stories.title: Taco Bell’s Office Lease Largest in Orange County, Calif., in Five Years
stories.excerpt: Orange County, Calif.’s office market improved again in the third quarter thanks to a diverse set of corporate leases. Total vacancy improved to 15.4 percent, down from 17.1 percent a year ago, while average asking rents increased to $3.02 per square foot per month, up from $2.90 at the end of 2025, according to new data from JLL. Net absorption slipped slightly for the quarter, but remained positive on the year at 265,394 square feet, compared to negative 158,099 square feet for all of 2025. Tenants signed about 1.55 million square feet of leases during the quarter, led by Taco Bell’s 254,162-square-foot lease at Irvine Company’s Alton HQ, the largest office lease signed in Orange County in five years. (The maker of the Crunchwrap Supreme plans to relocate from its current Irvine headquarters in 2028.) Medical device maker Envista Holdings also signed for 101,800 square feet across three buildings, while an unnamed aerospace company took 173,057 square feet across two Airport Area properties, including 102,417 square feet at 4000 MacArthur Boulevard. The South County submarket posted the strongest quarterly absorption at 86,107 square feet, with Irvine Company’s Irvine Spectrum campus contributing 133,115 square feet. However, several other submarkets posted losses in absorption. Supply remains tight as Orange County has recorded no new office completions so far this year, and only one project — the 168,137-square-foot building underway at the Anaheim Ducks’ $5 billion mixed-use development — is under construction. The project is expected to deliver in the fourth quarter, and is already 23 percent pre-leased. Office conversions are also removing space from the market. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Taco Bell leases 254K SF at Irvine Company's Alton HQ (Orange County, CA)—largest OC office lease in 5 years.
Orange County office vacancy fell to 15.4% (Q3 2025); asking rents rose to $3.02/SF/month; YTD absorption +265K SF.
Relocation planned for 2028; other Q3 leases: Envista 101.8K SF, aerospace tenant 173K SF across two sites.
stories.summary: Taco Bell has signed a 254,162-square-foot lease at Irvine Company's Alton HQ, the largest office lease in Orange County in five years, with relocation planned for 2028. Orange County's office market tightened significantly: vacancy fell to 15.4% (from 17.1% year-over-year), rents rose to $3.02/SF/month (from $2.90 year-end 2025), and positive net absorption rebounded to 265,394 SF year-to-date. Additional notable Q3 tenants included medical device maker Envista (101.8K SF) and an aerospace company (173K SF).
stories.impact: Taco Bell HQ relocation signals Irvine's strength as a tech/corporate services hub; influx of white-collar office tenants and their payroll bases will drive young-professional renter demand in Orange County coastal and I-405 corridor submarkets, supporting market-rate multifamily development in Irvine, Newport Beach, and Costa Mesa—particularly near tech parks and transit nodes.

stories.title: Yves Saint Laurent to Open Store at Kering’s 717 Fifth Avenue
stories.excerpt: Luxury French fashion house Yves Saint Laurent will open a new store at 717 Fifth Avenue, a new report revealed. According to a market report released by CBRE, the Kering-owned fashion house, once known as YSL for its founder, the late Yves Saint Laurent, will open in nearly 9,600 square feet in the base of the former Corning Glass Building that sits across East 56th Street from Trump Tower. Saint Laurent is currently at 3 East 57th Street, where it opened in 2003. That store was expanded to 14,071 square feet and renovated in 2015. According to property records, the original lease on East 57th Street ended in 2022 and had no renewal options. Since the fashion retailer is still there, the company likely signed a five-year extension during the pandemic, which would come due in October 2027. The building is managed by Buchbinder & Warren, which did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Kering bought the lower four floors at 717 Fifth Avenue in January 2024 for $963 million from Jeff Sutton’s Wharton Properties and SL Green Realty. The condominium has about 110,000 square feet that encompasses three floors of retail and one office floor. Most of the retail is occupied by Dolce & Gabbana and Armani. In December 2025, facing financial pressure, Kering sold a 60 percent stake to the large French private equity investment firm, Ardian, revaluing the commercial condominium to $900 million at $7,830 per square foot, but giving Kering a $690 million cash boost. It was expected at the time that Kering would begin to bring its own brands under its roof. Along with Saint Laurent, Kering encompasses Gucci, Balenciaga, Bottega Veneta, McQueen, Brioni plus Boucheron, Pomellato, DoDo, Qeelin, Ginori 1735 as well as Kering Eyewear. bullets: Yves Saint Laurent opens 9.6K SF flagship at Kering's 717 Fifth Avenue (Manhattan base); relocates from East 57th.
Current YSL lease (East 57th Street) ends October 2027; original lease ended 2022 with no renewal option.
Kering purchased 717 Fifth lower four floors for $963M (Jan. 2024) from Sutton/SL Green; controls street-front luxury retail.
stories.summary: Yves Saint Laurent is relocating its Manhattan flagship from 3 East 57th Street (14,071 SF) to 9,600 square feet at the base of 717 Fifth Avenue, Kering's $963 million acquisition from January 2024. The East 57th Street original lease ended in 2022 without renewal options; YSL likely signed a pandemic-era five-year extension expiring October 2027. Kering now controls the Fifth Avenue street frontage and lower floors, consolidating luxury brand portfolio presence.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact; consolidation of luxury fashion flagships by Kering at trophy Fifth Avenue locations reflects capital concentration in ultra-prime retail rather than secondary CBD—suggests constrained retail leasing velocity outside Manhattan's most exclusive corridors, reducing spillover demand for nearby hotel/mixed-use development.

stories.title: Northern Virginia Office Vacancy Falls Again as AI, Defense Demand Builds
stories.excerpt: Northern Virginia’s office market continued to tighten in the third quarter as more demand from artificial intelligence, technology and defense tenants bolstered weaker leasing activity. The market posted 672,378 square feet of positive net absorption during the quarter, reversing losses from the first half of the year tied to buildings being removed from the market, according to JLL. The National Science Foundation’s 380,000-square-foot move to 401 Dulany Street accounted for much of the gain. Northern Virginia’s office vacancy rate fell for a sixth straight quarter to 21.7 percent. Total available space dropped to 33.6 million square feet, its lowest level in a decade, and 25.5 percent below the 45.1 million-square-foot peak in 2023. Leasing activity slowed to just 1.3 million square feet on the quarter, with no deals of more than 100,000 square feet. AI, technology and defense companies committed to more than 300,000 square feet of net new space. And defense spending and tech investment are expected to continue driving momentum. Relocations and new leases have accounted for 58 percent of leasing so far in 2026 in a reverse to the renewal era of 2021 through 2023. Office supply is beginning to strengthen rents, according to JLL. Class A direct asking rents reached $42.51 per square foot per year, while overall direct asking rents averaged $38.13. JLL’s longer-term data shows asking rents have risen since 2022 for Trophy, Class A and Class B properties, while Class C rents have slipped. New construction remains virtually nonexistent, with only about 34,000 square feet underway. Meanwhile, more than 10 million square feet of existing office inventory has been proposed for redevelopment, a dynamic JLL expects will continue tightening the lower end of the market while limited Trophy supply pushes demand toward Class A properties. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Northern Virginia office vacancy fell to 21.7% (Q3 2025, 6th straight quarter decline); total available space at 10-year low.
National Science Foundation 380K SF move to 401 Dulany Street drove Q3 absorption of 672.4K SF (reversing H1 losses).
AI, technology, defense tenants committed 300K+ SF net new; defense spend and tech investment expected to sustain momentum.
stories.summary: Northern Virginia's office market tightened significantly in Q3 2025, with vacancy falling to 21.7% for the sixth consecutive quarter. Total available space dropped to 33.6 million square feet, the lowest in a decade and 25.5% below the 2023 peak. The National Science Foundation's relocation of 380,000 square feet to 401 Dulany Street accounted for much of the 672,378 SF of positive net absorption; AI, technology, and defense tenants committed over 300,000 SF of net new space, expected to continue driving market tightness.
stories.impact: Sustained demand from NSF, AI/ML companies, and defense contractors in Northern Virginia will accelerate wage growth and young-professional in-migration to Tysons, Reston, Herndon, and Arlington submarkets; multifamily developers should acquire infill and edge-of-employment-center land in Northern Virginia now before competition intensifies and land/construction costs inflate—window to build class-A workforce housing ahead of tech/defense talent influx is closing.
